FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.problem: The three house-name pdf_text_style checks will often test the wrong placement. In verify_outputs.py, pdf_text_style returns on the FIRST page where the text appears, and on that page it reads the first match in content-stream order. The brochure has to name each house in several places: section headings, the photo captions the commission requires ("photographs labelled by villa"), and usually a comparison table or summary. The page order is left to the designer ("the brochure's comparison sequence"). Any of those mentions can come before the heading. I ran the checks on the 2026-09-28 run brochure: "Casa Oliveto" also appears on p5 (comparison table) and p6 (summary), in smaller sizes. If the comparison page or a captioned photo comes first, a compliant brochure fails the 34 pt check. With H042 retired, nothing reliably tests the 34 pt house-name heading.
FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.fix: Remove bro-style-oliveto, bro-style-scogliera and bro-style-verranza: the text is fixed, but the placement is ambiguous inside one file. Un-retire H042 and change its wording to: "Each house name heading in “Villa comparison brochure” (villa-collection.pdf) is set at 34 pt, not counting its enlarged initial." Point T01's villa-collection cell to H035 and H042. If you keep the autos, add a "page" field, but page order is a designer choice, so this does not work as a general fix. The nine rate autos (bro-rate-*) are safer, because every rate in the brochure is meant to be 9 pt. Keep them.

FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.problem: H028 was modified to drop "and is set larger than them" because code now checks the sizes. That size relationship was the only visible-hierarchy fact on the brochure. It now depends entirely on the 34 pt and 9 pt autos. Those raise not-assessable when the text is outlined: the export setting says only "searchable text where practical", so outlined lettering is allowed. The house-name autos are also unreliable (finding 1). So the fact can quietly disappear.

FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.problem: The palette distribution rule says the three accents together cover "no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area". FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.problem: The patch took two items from the owner_note.txt do-not-want list and added checks on all four outputs: no fake evening glow (B16) and no crushed blacks (B17). It left out the item about stone: "No stone turned into a computer's idea of stone". BR02's checks (H011, H009, H004, H014, H021, H027) test walls, openings and features, meaning geometry. They do not test whether the surface texture was smoothed, painted or re-rendered. So one do-not-want item has no check on any output, while its two siblings got checks.

FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.problem: The modified opacity checks now say every "panel, button and mark" is "solid colour at full opacity, with no tint, transparency, gradient or shadow". Two gaps against the brand rule. First, the brand rule explicitly lets supplied raster artwork keep its edge anti-aliasing, and a strict reader could fail an anti-aliased monogram as not "solid colour". Second, B07 lists "blend mode" but no cited check mentions it. These checks are also the evidence for B15 (artwork at 100% layer opacity).
FIDELITY AND COVERAGE.fix: Use this wording: "Every panel and button on “…” (file) is solid colour at full opacity, with no tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode; any monogram is placed at 100% opacity." Apply it to the same four ids.
